local_bottleneck: INGO registration needs a partnering line-ministry MoU, a Rwandan office structure and a named local representative
deduction: Donations to registered/qualified institutions deductible; modest cap (30% of tax base)
foreign_donor_restriction: No FCRA-style ban, but INGOs need funding-commitment proof, ministry MoU and RGB monitoring/revocation powers
corrections: Regulator is now Rwanda Governance Board (RGB), successor to MIDRRP; Law 01/2016 governs NGOs; official fee 300,000 RWF (~$24)

local_bottleneck: Foreign associations need prior government approval (Ministry of Interior/Humanitarian Affairs), local representative and office; high refusal/suspension risk
deduction: Limited/donor incentives not well established for foreign donors
foreign_donor_restriction: Foreign NGOs periodically suspended by security council (e.g. 2021) and required to re-register; approvals discretionary and political
corrections: Governing law is Law 02/2017 on associations (plus 2017 ministerial ordinances); confirms very hard and politically risky

local_bottleneck: Foreign NGO must have a Ugandan-resident legal representative, local office and route funds via Ugandan bank accounts
deduction: Donations to registered NGOs deductible, capped at 10% of tax base
foreign_donor_restriction: No ban, but NGO/CSO Act 2016 ties foreign funding to registration, bank-account reporting and source-of-funds disclosure
corrections: Confirm prior: NGO/CSO Act 2016, National NGO Bureau (ngobureau.go.ug), resident legal rep + local bank account requirements

local_bottleneck: NGO Commission registration requires local office and international NGOs need 5+ members incl. at least 2 Tanzanians
deduction: Donor tax deductions limited; registered NGOs largely tax-exempt on revenue
foreign_donor_restriction: Foreign-funded NGOs register with NGO Commission; funding thresholds and reporting monitored; no outright ban
corrections: Core law is NGO Act (No. 22 of 2002, as amended); the 2021 tightening was a draft NGO Bill, not enacted law - earlier '2021 amendments' note overstated

local_bottleneck: Foreign PBOs need Kenyan-resident officers and a Kenya office; PBORA registration via eCitizen
fee_usd: ~$40-100 (PBORA registration, name reservation KES 1,000; old NGO Act KES 100,000 deposit no longer the route)
deduction: Donations to registered PBOs deductible; 30% of tax base cap
foreign_donor_restriction: No FCRA-style ban; foreign PBOs must register with PBORA, keep Kenya office and file annual reports
corrections: NGO Act 2003 was repealed - current framework is PBO Act, 2013 (Cap 134) under PBORA, not the NGO Commission/NGO Act route

local_bottleneck: Foreign associations need prior government authorization (Art. 9, Law 86-006/AF) and 2020 agrément decree with local representative and office
deduction: No meaningful donor deduction regime established
foreign_donor_restriction: Prior authorization mandatory; agrément (decret 20-101/PR, 2020) granted by Ministry of Foreign Affairs; civil-society space restricted
corrections: Main legal basis is Law 86-006/AF (1986) art. 9 plus Decree 20-101/PR of 31 July 2020 on NGO agrément; prior '2019 NGO law' reference is inaccurate

local_bottleneck: Foreign NGOs need an 'accord de siege' (headquarters authorization) from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs plus local representative/office
time_to_register: 2-6 months (agrément decision target 2 months per Decree 98-711)
deduction: Donor deductions limited; registered NGOs can be tax-exempted
foreign_donor_restriction: No FCRA-style ban; foreign NGOs accredited (agrément) under Law 96-030 with MFA involvement; no local-citizenship board rule
corrections: Confirm prior; core law is Law 96-030 (1996) + Decree 98-711; MFA accord de siege route confirmed by French diplomatic services page

local_bottleneck: International NGOs must register with the NGO Registrar and have a Zambian office and local representative
deduction: Donations to registered charitable institutions deductible; ~30% of tax base cap
foreign_donor_restriction: No FCRA-style restriction; international NGOs register under the Act with standard reporting
corrections: Governing law is NGO Act No. 16 of 2009 (not 2005); Registrar sits in Ministry of Community Development and Social Services
